claims.text: The famous Avenue des Champs-Élysées stretches an impressive 1.9 kilometres in length and 70 metres in width.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Its grand name translates to the 'Elysian Fields', which is the resting place for dead heroes in ancient Greek mythology.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Before it became an avenue, the land here was surprisingly occupied by simple fields and kitchen gardens until the reign of Louis XIV.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: It was originally laid out in 1667 by André Le Nôtre simply as a tree-lined extension of the Tuileries Garden.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The new wide boulevard was initially called the 'Grand Cours' and did not officially take its current name until 1709.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Today, it famously serves as the prestigious finish line for the Tour de France cycling race and the route for the annual Bastille Day military parade.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Lined with luxury shops, cafés, and theatres, it has often been described as the most beautiful avenue in the whole world.
claims.subject: self
